transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, it's mostly because... people keep telling me I'm not listening. Like, my supervisor at the plant, or my wife. They'll be talking right at me, looking me in the eye, and... a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, which really sets my wife off. She hates repeating herself. Actually, we got into a huge fight about it last weekend when we were supposed to go to her sister's house. Her sister lives out in Springfield, you know, past the old mall they tore down? They're building some new apartment complex there now, but honestly, the traffic on that road is just terrible since they started the construction. I don't even know why they approved that zoning. But yeah, anyway, I just... I miss things people say to me.

{"intent": "Determine whether the difficulty is due to physical hearing impairment or inattention", "question": "When you miss what people are saying, do you have trouble physically hearing the sounds, or

No, my hearing is fine. I hear the actual sounds perfectly. We actually have to get our hearing checked every single year at the plant because of the noise levels on the floor. They bring in this little white trailer, and you sit in this tiny soundproof booth with headphones, and you just press a button when you hear a beep. I always pass it no problem. 

The real issue is the earplugs they make us wear—they're those cheap orange foam ones that expand in your ear? They itch so bad. I was telling my buddy Mike we should just buy our own custom ones. Mike goes to the shooting range a lot, so he has these really nice molded ones. He’s got this crazy collection of vintage rifles, actually. We were supposed to go to a gun show together last month but his truck broke down. It’s a Chevy, and I told him the transmission on those years was notoriously bad, but... wait, sorry, what were we talking about? 

Oh, right. Yeah, I hear people just fine, it's just like my brain isn't recording the words.
Did you have similar trouble paying attention or staying focused back when you were in elementary school?

Yeah, oh yeah. I was definitely like this as a kid. I mean, my mom used to say I had a motor attached to me. In elementary school, the teachers were always moving my desk around because I just couldn't stay put. I'd be up sharpening my pencil, or looking out the window, or... oh, man, I remember in third grade, Mrs. Gable's class, she put my desk right up against her desk so she could keep an eye on me. Mrs. Gable, she was this really strict older lady, always wore these bright floral dresses. She actually smelled like peppermints all the time. I think she kept a stash of them in her top drawer. I love peppermints, actually, the soft ones that melt in your mouth, not the hard ones that break your teeth. I cracked a molar on a hard candy once at a movie theater. It was that new action movie with the car chases, you know the one? The special effects were amazing, but anyway, the dental bill was ridiculous. 

But yeah, back in school, before middle school even, I was always getting in trouble. I'd just blurt out the answers before anyone else could raise their hand, or I'd be leaning over into the next kid's desk, butting into their work because I was bored with mine. They just couldn't keep me in my seat.
Nowadays as an adult, do you still feel physically restless or have trouble sitting still?

Yeah, I do. It's... it's like this pressure building up inside my chest and my legs. If I have to sit still for too long, like in a meeting or something, I feel like I've just got to move or do something right that second, or I'm gonna crawl right out of my skin. 

It's actually why I like working the floor at the plant, honestly. I get to walk the line, check the machines. We use these massive hydraulic presses, and the vibration they make when they stamp the metal is wild. You can feel it in your boots. I had to buy new steel-toes last month because the soles on my old ones completely wore out from all the walking. I got them at Red Wing—man, those guys really know how to fit a boot. The guy there, I think his name was Jerry, he was telling me about how he used to work construction out in Colorado before he moved back here. Colorado's supposed to be beautiful. My wife wants to go there for our anniversary, maybe rent a cabin in the mountains. She found this place online that has a hot tub out on the deck, which sounds great, but I don't know if I could just sit in a hot tub for hours like she does. 

But yeah, sitting still is... it's just really hard for me. I always end up bouncing my leg or pacing if I have to be in one place too long.
